gap: No result ChatGPT got names who timed any chamber or says how. CNC Kitchen (Stefan Hermann) put thermocouples in a European 230 V Bambu Lab X2D and measured a real 65 °C in about 20 minutes with the chamber heater alone. He says running the heated bed too roughly halves that, and US 110–120 V units will likely take longer. On the H2D he timed about 10 minutes to 60 °C with bed and heater together, also on a 230 V machine.
standout_why: I compared against the cited QIDI Plus 4 TechSpecs page, desktop3dprinters.us chamber-temperature-specs and 3dcalculators.com heat-3d-printer-enclosure. The yakja.co comparison would not load (certificate error), so I could not check it. The QIDI page lists 400 W and 65 °C but no times. The desktop3dprinters table lists only maximum chamber temperatures and gives no times. 3dcalculators gives QIDI Plus4 times only: about 8 minutes from a 3DJake listing, about 5 minutes from QIDI's own blog, and 16.5 minutes to print-ready from an owner test. ChatGPT's answer showed the X2D at '~20 min to 65°C (reported)' and the H2S at '~25 min' with no named measurer. The rival pages lack the thermocouple method, the fact that running the bed halves the time, the 230 V vs 120 V caveat for US buyers, and any named H2D measurement. The H2S's ~25 minutes traces to bambuhub.net, which publishes it as setup guidance, not a test.
decides: This partly undermines ChatGPT's pick. The only named, instrumented chamber timings I could open are for the Bambu Lab X2D and H2D. The QIDI Plus4's '5 minutes to ~60 °C' is from QIDI's own blog and names no tester or conditions. So the Plus4-vs-X2D comparison sets a vendor claim against a heater-only thermocouple test on a 230 V European unit, which is not a fair head-to-head. With the bed on as well, CNC Kitchen's numbers put the X2D at roughly 10 minutes and the H2D at about 10 minutes to 60 °C. Both figures come from 230 V machines, and a US shopper's 120 V unit is likely slower. The page should say plainly that no named reviewer has timed the QIDI Plus4, QIDI Plus5, Creality K2 Plus or Bambu H2S under the same conditions, so 'fastest' cannot be crowned from measurements.

findings.label: Chamber heat-up to 65 °C, chamber heater only (measured)
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab X2D Review: Dual Nozzle, One Catch (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann)
findings.note: Published 2026-04-14. Hermann 'placed some thermocouples into the chamber'; the article does not give the sensor positions. Heated bed was off. He says running the bed as well 'cuts the heat-up time roughly in half' (about 10 min, his estimate). His unit is the 230 V European version, and he says 'if you get a US version, your heat-up times will likely be longer.' He measured total draw at over 1,500 W.

findings.label: Chamber heat-up to 60 °C, bed and chamber heater together (measured)
findings.source_title: I Tested the Bambu Lab H2D (CNC Kitchen, Stefan Hermann)
findings.note: Published 2025-03-25. Tested on a 230 V machine. He says '110V' machines 'might be slower' because of their 'considerably lower maximum power rating compared to the 2200W available in 230V regions.' He also found the bed about 10 °C below its setpoint with a thermal camera and a thermocouple; Bambu later fixed this in firmware.
